title: Separate syntax from row errors
brief: Import malformed JSON followed by valid JSON containing one invalid project row.
explanation: A parser failure and a domain validation failure require different locations and recovery advice.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import malformed JSON followed by valid JSON containing one invalid project row. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Create distinct typed results for file parsing and row decoding.
Feed both fixtures through the same upload operation. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The malformed file reports syntax context without attempting row writes.
The valid file identifies the invalid row and field precisely.
Recovery evidence: Truncate a file halfway through its final object. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Truncate a file halfway through its final object.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the UI avoid inventing row numbers when parsing never succeeded?
stretch: Add an editor link to the exact byte or line location when available.

experiment: Provide a nested object with unexpected prototype-related keys.

stretch: Add safe unknown-key handling and document strip-versus-reject behavior.

brief: Feed a very large CSV field whose opening quote is never closed.
explanation: Malformed input should terminate with bounded diagnostics rather than endless accumulation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Feed a very large CSV field whose opening quote is never closed. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Set file and field limits and stop parsing when a declared limit is exceeded.
Track consumed bytes and emitted errors for the malformed fixture. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The importer reports the specific limit or unmatched quote.
It never freezes the interface while retaining an unbounded field buffer.
Recovery evidence: Cancel parsing near the configured limit. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Cancel parsing near the configured limit.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are limits enforced during parsing rather than after allocating everything?
stretch: Add a worker parser with progress based on consumed bytes.

title: Test delimiter detection ambiguity
brief: Upload a small file containing both commas and semicolons in unquoted text.
explanation: Automatic dialect detection can be ambiguous and must expose uncertainty.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Upload a small file containing both commas and semicolons in unquoted text. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Score candidate dialects and require a visible selection when no clear fit exists.
Preview the same bytes under both candidate delimiters. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The user sees the resulting column interpretation before committing.
The importer never silently chooses a destructive mapping.
Recovery evidence: Change the selected dialect after resolving row errors. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change the selected dialect after resolving row errors.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the preview clearly bind its errors to the current dialect?
stretch: Persist a trusted dialect choice only for an explicit named import source.

title: Chunk validation without freezing
brief: Validate fifty thousand small rows while the user types in a search field.
explanation: Large validation work needs bounded chunks so the interface remains responsive.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Validate fifty thousand small rows while the user types in a search field. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Process a measured chunk and yield between chunks or move parsing to a worker.
Record input responsiveness and total processed rows during validation. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Typing and cancel controls remain usable throughout the import.
Chunking never skips or validates a row twice.
Recovery evidence: Slow the validator deliberately and repeat the interaction. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Slow the validator deliberately and repeat the interaction.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Is progress driven by completed work rather than a decorative timer?
stretch: Compare worker and main-thread chunking with the same deterministic fixture.

title: Cancel the current parse only
brief: Start parsing file A, select file B, and cancel the visible parse.
explanation: Cancellation must target the active operation and prevent obsolete results from surfacing.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Start parsing file A, select file B, and cancel the visible parse. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Associate each parse with an identity and owned cancellation handle.
Resolve file A after file B has become current. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Only file B's current status can update the preview.
A late result from A cannot resurrect its commit button.
Recovery evidence: Cancel B immediately before its completion message arrives. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Cancel B immediately before its completion message arrives.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does cleanup distinguish supersession from user-visible parse failure?
stretch: Add a recent-file history without retaining obsolete mutable previews.

title: Virtualize preview rows accessibly
brief: Preview one hundred thousand valid records with a keyboard-navigable error list.
explanation: Rendering cost should depend on the visible window while row identity remains stable.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Preview one hundred thousand valid records with a keyboard-navigable error list. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Window the table and provide an accessible route to offscreen error rows.
Jump to row ninety thousand and edit its mapping. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The selected row keeps its source identity after scrolling.
Virtualization never changes the commit target set.
Recovery evidence: Change sorting while an offscreen row is selected. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change sorting while an offscreen row is selected.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does keyboard focus survive recycled DOM elements?
stretch: Offer a paginated accessible alternative to the virtualized preview.

title: Bound concurrent enrichment
brief: Validate rows using an optional remote lookup limited to four simultaneous requests.
explanation: Concurrency limits protect the dependency and must cover retries as well as initial calls.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Validate rows using an optional remote lookup limited to four simultaneous requests. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Use a bounded worker pool and record active-request high-water marks.
Import twenty rows with delayed lookup responses. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: At most four lookups are active at any time.
Retries cannot create extra uncounted concurrent requests.
Recovery evidence: Make one lookup hang until its timeout. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Make one lookup hang until its timeout.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does releasing a permit happen on success, failure, and interruption?
stretch: Add per-host limits when enrichment calls multiple providers.

title: Report monotonic progress
brief: Parse bytes, validate rows, and commit records as three separate import phases.
explanation: Percentages need an honest denominator and cannot imply durability before commit.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Parse bytes, validate rows, and commit records as three separate import phases. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Show phase-specific progress with known totals where available.
Observe progress during unknown-length parsing and a later failed commit. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Progress never decreases within a completed phase.
Validation at one hundred percent never claims data is already saved.
Recovery evidence: Change estimated row count as more bytes are parsed. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Change estimated row count as more bytes are parsed.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Did the agent blend incomparable byte and row counts into one misleading metric?
stretch: Add an elapsed-time estimate labeled as approximate and independent of correctness.

title: Release canceled buffers
brief: Select and cancel a large import five times without reloading the app.
explanation: Canceled operations must release buffers, listeners, and worker references they own.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Select and cancel a large import five times without reloading the app. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Dispose worker subscriptions and clear obsolete parse artifacts on cancellation.
Measure retained references after each cancel cycle. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Retained memory settles near the baseline after cleanup.
Old workers cannot post messages into the active preview.
Recovery evidence: Cancel while a worker transfers a large result buffer. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Cancel while a worker transfers a large result buffer.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Are ownership and cleanup explicit for transferred buffers?
stretch: Expose development counters for active parsers and retained preview plans.

title: Separate validation from commit batching
brief: A million-row import cannot fit comfortably into one long transaction.
explanation: Batching improves responsiveness but changes recovery semantics unless staged carefully.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A million-row import cannot fit comfortably into one long transaction. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Choose staging-plus-swap or resumable partial commit and describe its guarantees.
Fail after several batches and inspect both visible and staged records. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The visible result follows the chosen atomic or resumable contract.
The UI never describes a partially committed import as rolled back.
Recovery evidence: Restart the browser before the final batch finishes. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Restart the browser before the final batch finishes.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the receipt support exact resumption without duplicate rows?
stretch: Benchmark staged import space cost alongside its stronger atomic visibility.

title: Apply backpressure to parsing
brief: A parser produces rows faster than asynchronous validation can consume them.
explanation: A queue must remain bounded when downstream work is slower than upstream input.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A parser produces rows faster than asynchronous validation can consume them. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Pause production or use a bounded handoff between parsing and validation.
Make validation ten times slower than parsing and measure queue depth. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Buffered rows remain within the configured limit.
The importer does not accumulate the whole file in an unbounded array.
Recovery evidence: Interrupt while the producer waits for queue capacity. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Interrupt while the producer waits for queue capacity.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can both producer and consumer terminate without deadlock?
stretch: Record queue depth and throughput to tune capacity with evidence.

title: Keep error pages bounded
brief: Ten thousand rows fail the same required-field rule during a large import.
explanation: The interface needs a count and navigable samples without mounting every error at once.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Ten thousand rows fail the same required-field rule during a large import. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Paginate issues with stable source indices and summary counts by code.
Navigate to the final issue page and export the full report. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Every issue remains reachable or exportable.
The first page does not falsely imply only its displayed issues exist.
Recovery evidence: Correct a row and rebuild the report while on a later page. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Correct a row and rebuild the report while on a later page.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does pagination clamp safely when the new issue total shrinks?
stretch: Provide a grouped fix suggestion that still preserves each source-row association.

title: Reject unknown future versions
brief: Import a backup marked schema version ninety-nine into a client supporting versions one through three.
explanation: A future contract cannot be safely guessed from familiar-looking fields.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import a backup marked schema version ninety-nine into a client supporting versions one through three. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Validate the version before dispatching to a version-specific decoder.
Attempt preview with the future version and otherwise valid rows. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The user receives a clear unsupported-version message.
No mutation or lossy best-effort downgrade occurs.
Recovery evidence: Remove the version marker and test the documented legacy rule. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Remove the version marker and test the documented legacy rule.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the decoder distinguish missing legacy version from unknown future version?
stretch: Provide an update link or export-conversion guidance appropriate to the app.

title: Adapt renamed fields
brief: Version one calls a field objective while version two calls it goal.
explanation: A version adapter should translate historical meaning before current-domain validation.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Version one calls a field objective while version two calls it goal. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Implement a version-one adapter with an explicit field mapping.
Restore fixtures containing only old, only new, and contradictory fields. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The supported old fixture produces the expected current goal.
Ambiguous mixed fields follow a documented conflict rule.
Recovery evidence: Give the old field an invalid nonstring value. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Give the old field an invalid nonstring value.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does adaptation preserve errors rather than coercing bad data into plausible text?
stretch: Record the original format version in the import receipt.

title: Keep canonical fixtures immutable
brief: A developer changes export formatting and updates every golden fixture automatically.
explanation: Fixtures are useful only when changes receive semantic review against compatibility promises.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A developer changes export formatting and updates every golden fixture automatically. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Separate historical input fixtures from current expected export fixtures.
Run all historical imports after the exporter change. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Old supported backups still restore equivalent records.
A bulk snapshot update cannot hide removed compatibility coverage.
Recovery evidence: Deliberately remove one legacy adapter and ensure a historical test fails. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Deliberately remove one legacy adapter and ensure a historical test fails.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does each fixture document the behavior it protects?
stretch: Attach a small human-readable manifest of expected entities to every historical fixture.

title: Handle added required fields
brief: Current tasks require a priority field absent from supported older backups.
explanation: A newly required field needs a version-specific migration rule rather than arbitrary UI defaults.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Current tasks require a priority field absent from supported older backups. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Supply a documented historical default during adaptation.
Import old rows and compare them with freshly created current rows. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Both satisfy the current domain schema with intentional values.
Missing current-version required fields are not excused as legacy data.
Recovery evidence: Label a malformed current file as old and inspect validation behavior. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Label a malformed current file as old and inspect validation behavior.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does version selection itself have a trustworthy envelope contract?
stretch: Add provenance metadata indicating fields supplied by compatibility defaults.

title: Define unknown-field policy
brief: Import a supported-version project row containing an extra experimental metadata property.
explanation: Unknown fields may be rejected, preserved, or stripped, but the choice must be explicit.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Import a supported-version project row containing an extra experimental metadata property. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Apply the policy at the version boundary and explain any data loss in preview.
Round-trip a row with unfamiliar nested metadata. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Behavior matches the documented preserve-or-strip decision.
Unknown properties never become executable configuration or unrestricted write fields.
Recovery evidence: Include an unexpected property that shadows a known method name. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Include an unexpected property that shadows a known method name.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does broad object spreading bypass the declared policy?
stretch: Offer a raw-source attachment when preserving unknown data is useful for later migration.

title: Version enum changes
brief: An older backup uses task status done while the current model uses complete.
explanation: Enum evolution needs explicit semantic mapping and rejection for unmapped values.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An older backup uses task status done while the current model uses complete. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Map supported historical statuses before current schema decoding.
Import done, complete, and an unknown abandoned status under each version. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Only documented mappings produce current valid states.
Unknown values are never coerced into a convenient default.
Recovery evidence: Add a new current status and rerun old export compatibility checks. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Add a new current status and rerun old export compatibility checks.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does changing a label accidentally change the persisted contract?
stretch: Keep display labels separate from stable serialized enum values.

title: Preserve stable identities across conversion
brief: Convert a version-one backup whose task IDs are referenced by evidence and dependencies.
explanation: A format adapter must update all references consistently if identity representation changes.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: Convert a version-one backup whose task IDs are referenced by evidence and dependencies. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Build an explicit identity map before translating related records.
Compare every converted reference against the resulting entity set. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: All links resolve to the intended converted task.
No converter generates independent new IDs for each reference occurrence.
Recovery evidence: Include two old IDs that would collide under naive normalization. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Include two old IDs that would collide under naive normalization.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the adapter detect collisions before producing a commit plan?
stretch: Emit a conversion report showing identity changes without exposing private content.

title: Negotiate export targets honestly
brief: A user requests a version-one export from data containing version-three-only dependency features.
explanation: Older formats may be unable to represent newer semantics without loss.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: A user requests a version-one export from data containing version-three-only dependency features. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
List unsupported features and require an explicit loss policy before conversion.
Export a fixture containing every newer feature. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: The artifact and warning accurately describe omitted or transformed data.
The app never labels a lossy export as a complete backup.
Recovery evidence: Restore the older artifact and compare the missing semantics. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Restore the older artifact and compare the missing semantics.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Can the interface distinguish interoperability export from recovery backup?
stretch: Offer a companion report preserving details the older format cannot encode.

title: Review compatibility as a release gate
brief: An agent refactors decoders and reports that the latest export still imports.
explanation: Current round-trip success does not establish support for historical contracts.
steps: Create a repeatable fixture: An agent refactors decoders and reports that the latest export still imports. Record the starting rows and relevant UI state before making the change.
Require the supported-version fixture matrix in the change review.
Run old imports, current round-trip, malformed input, and future-version rejection. Exercise the real operation boundary as well as the rendered result.
checks: Every promised version retains its documented behavior.
Removing a supported adapter fails a meaningful release check.
Recovery evidence: Introduce a renamed field without updating its old-version adapter. Record the resulting state and prove that a fresh valid action still works.
experiment: Introduce a renamed field without updating its old-version adapter.
review: Review the agent's proposed diff: Does the PR explain any intentional support-policy change?
stretch: Generate a compatibility matrix from fixture metadata for release documentation.
